UnitStatement: OpenPipeStress agentic development uses a flat project hierarchy.
The hierarchy nests PKG-XX Package above DEL-XX-YY Deliverable, rooted at execution/_Decomposition/SOFTWARE_DECOMP.md.
There are no phases, sub-packages, or task sub-levels inside deliverables.
Delivery sequencing may be managed separately; package identity is a domain partition, not a schedule phase.
Scope Item uses format SOW-NNN (e.g., SOW-003) and is assigned by SOFTWARE_DECOMP.
Objective uses format OBJ-NNN (e.g., OBJ-001) and is assigned by SOFTWARE_DECOMP.
Package uses format PKG-XX (e.g., PKG-04) and is assigned by SOFTWARE_DECOMP.
Deliverable uses format DEL-XX-YY (e.g., DEL-04-02) and is assigned by SOFTWARE_DECOMP.
Decision uses format DEC-NNN (e.g., DEC-001) and is assigned by a human or Type 1 agent draft.
Open Issue uses format OI-NNN (e.g., OI-004) and is assigned by Type 1 agent draft or human.
Risk uses format RISK-NNN (e.g., RISK-002) and is assigned by Type 1 agent draft or human.
Deliverable IDs are coupled to package IDs: DEL-04-02 belongs to PKG-04.
Stable identifiers persist across renames.
DOC_UPDATE deliverable type covers documentation, policy, guide, or report-template work.
DATA_MODEL_CHANGE deliverable type covers schema, type, serialization, or domain object change.
API_CONTRACT deliverable type covers public API, plugin, import/export, or data contract.
BACKEND_FEATURE_SLICE deliverable type covers bounded backend/core behavior implementation.
UX_UI_SLICE deliverable type covers a bounded GUI feature or view.
TEST_SUITE deliverable type covers verification, regression, validation, or lint suite.
CI_CD_CHANGE deliverable type covers build, packaging, release, or pipeline change.
SECURITY_CONTROL deliverable type covers privacy, redaction, storage, telemetry, or security control.
MODEL_INCOMPLETE status means required physical data for solving is missing; authority level is a software finding.
MECHANICS_SOLVED status means the numerical mechanics solve completed; authority level is solver result only.
RULE_INPUTS_INCOMPLETE status means mechanics may be solved but rule-pack required values are missing; authority level is a rule-pack finding.
USER_RULE_CHECKED status means a user-defined rule pack evaluated the result; authority is software computation using user data.
USER_RULE_FAILED status means a user-defined rule pack produced a failing result; authority is software computation using user data.
HUMAN_REVIEW_REQUIRED status means the result requires competent engineering review before reliance; always true for professional use.
HUMAN_APPROVED_FOR_PROJECT status means a human recorded project-specific acceptance outside the solver core; it is a human record only.
Automatic software-emitted statuses are limited to MODEL_INCOMPLETE, MECHANICS_SOLVED, RULE_INPUTS_INCOMPLETE, USER_RULE_CHECKED, USER_RULE_FAILED, and HUMAN_REVIEW_REQUIRED.
The software must not use HUMAN_APPROVED_FOR_PROJECT, CODE_COMPLIANT, CERTIFIED, SEALED, APPROVED, or equivalent professional/code-compliance language as an automatic status.
The code-neutral analysis boundary is the data-model surface that keeps the analysis statuses from collapsing into one another.

schemas/analysis_boundary.schema.yaml requires an explicit authority model: mechanics statuses from solver results, user-rule statuses from user-supplied rule-pack computation, and human acceptance as an external hash-bound project record only.
FACT epistemic label means directly observed in a cited source or model artifact.
ASSUMPTION epistemic label means a reasonable inference requiring human validation.
PROPOSAL epistemic label means a suggested design/development move requiring decision.
TBD epistemic label means unknown or unwarranted; must be resolved before reliance.
Current dependency registers use the canonical v3.1 core enum values defined by the shared Chirality dependency schema.
For write-form rows, DependencyType is limited to PREREQUISITE, INTERFACE, HANDOVER, CONSTRAINT, ENABLES, and OTHER.
For write-form rows, Status is limited to ACTIVE and RETIRED.
Candidate or non-gating graph questions are recorded in a candidate worklist or review packet, not as Status=CANDIDATE.

Legacy values from DAG-001 through DAG-006, including labels such as ARCHITECTURE_BASIS, DOMAIN_MODEL, GUI_PREDECESSOR, RUNNER_CONTRACT, INFERRED_DIRECT, UNKNOWN, and AnchorType=DELIVERABLE, are historical read-compatibility inputs only.
New or refreshed dependency artifacts must emit canonical enum values and preserve any legacy label in notes or a non-core extension field.
Open Mechanics is public analytical mechanics implemented by the solver: geometry, stiffness, loads, stress recovery, units, reports; may be shipped publicly.

Protected Standards Data is code text, tables, figures, code-derived formulas, allowables, SIF/flexibility tables, and protected dimensional tables; must not be shipped publicly unless explicit redistribution rights exist.
User-Supplied Code Data is values, formulas, allowables, SIFs, flexibility factors, load combinations, and interpretations entered by the user; may be stored in private project/rule-pack files.
Mechanics Solve is a solved numerical model with displacements, reactions, forces, moments, and mechanical stresses; not equivalent to a code check.
Rule-Pack Check is a user-defined expression/comparison applied to solver outputs; not equivalent to professional authentication.
Professional Approval is human acceptance for reliance by a competent/responsible professional; outside software authority.
Centerline Model is a 3D line-element representation of the piping centerline and components; the default global analysis model.

Frame Kernel is the code-neutral 3D frame mechanics core owning DOF ordering, element stiffness, transforms, assembly, boundary-condition reduction, and a bounded solve interface; it consumes unit-checked numeric inputs and does not perform rule checks or professional approval.

Solver Diagnostic is a deterministic mechanics-solver finding for singularity, invalid topology/restraints, numeric invalidity, conditioning, nonconvergence, or unresolved solver configuration; not a rule-pack result, code-compliance statement, or professional acceptance.
Local FEA Handoff is a transfer package for local shell/solid analysis; a specialized workflow, not the default global solver.

Plugin Manifest is a declared extension metadata record requesting entrypoints, permissions, provenance, privacy posture, checksums, sandbox requirements, and no-bypass constraints; a manifest grants nothing by itself.

Extension Point is a governed boundary where a plugin or adapter may request to import, export, validate, report, emit diagnostics, or expose user-owned rule-pack metadata; exact loader and transport remain TBD.

Domain Surface is the model, persistence, unit, analysis-boundary, rule-pack metadata, result, report, or diagnostic surface touched by an extension entrypoint; must be declared in the plugin manifest.

No-Bypass Constraint is a mandatory control plugins and adapters must preserve, including units, provenance, privacy, protected-content, diagnostics, hashes, rule sandboxing, reports, solver boundaries, and human acceptance boundaries; cannot be waived by plugin code.
USER_SUPPLIED_LICENSED_CODE provenance label means the user entered a value from a licensed code/standard.
USER_SUPPLIED_OWNER_SPEC provenance label means the user entered a value from owner/company design basis.
MANUFACTURER_PUBLIC_PERMISSIVE provenance label means manufacturer data with documented redistribution rights.
MANUFACTURER_PRIVATE provenance label means manufacturer/vendor data for private project use only.
PUBLIC_DOMAIN_OR_ORIGINAL provenance label means public-domain/original/invented data safe for public examples.
UNKNOWN_SOURCE provenance label means the source is not documented and cannot be relied on without review.
PROTECTED_CONTENT_SUSPECTED provenance label means quarantine and escalate before public use.
The canonical machine-readable domain model is schemas/model.schema.yaml, using JSON Schema 2020-12, written as strict JSON in a .yaml path, and intentionally code-neutral.

schemas/model.schema.yaml defines public object structure, identifiers, references, unit-bearing values, provenance, diagnostics, results, and report settings, but does not bundle protected standards data, proprietary catalog values, code-specific allowables, SIF/flexibility tables, or compliance rules.
PKG-02 owns the canonical semantic dimension vocabulary used by both schemas/units.schema.yaml DimensionId and schemas/model.schema.yaml Quantity.dimension.

The canonical semantic dimension vocabulary includes dimensionless, length, mass, time, temperature, temperature_interval, angle, rotation, force, force_per_length, moment, pressure, stress, area, volume, density, linear_stiffness, rotational_stiffness, displacement, velocity, acceleration, thermal_conductivity, specific_heat, thermal_expansion_coefficient, second_moment_area, section_modulus, mass_per_length, volume_per_length, slope, and TBD.

Retired dimension aliases are not accepted canonical enum values: use temperature_interval instead of temperature_difference, second_moment_area instead of area_moment, and classify generic stiffness as linear_stiffness or rotational_stiffness.
Unit catalogs, conversion constants, tolerances, code-specific values, release claims, and professional claims remain out of scope for the dimension vocabulary.

Project object is the project container for units, privacy/storage posture, models, rule-pack references, report settings, reports, diagnostics, and hashes; project-private engineering data remains user controlled unless intentionally contributed with documented rights.

Model object is a physical or derived analytical model container for nodes, elements, components, materials, sections, supports, load cases, combinations, results, diagnostics, unresolved assumptions, traceability links, and references to design knowledge, constraints, operations, states/runs, comparisons, handoff packages, and external metadata.

The Model physical_source_of_truth role anchors editable design data; downstream PKG-13 through PKG-16 contracts own detailed records and must not bypass canonical units, provenance, diagnostics, or professional-boundary controls.

ModelRole is a schema enum distinguishing a physical source-of-truth model from an analytical solver model, derived view, or unresolved TBD role; it is not a lifecycle or professional-approval status.

DesignKnowledgeEnvelope holds schema-first records for user-supplied endpoints, line data, routing corridors, zones, equipment interfaces, access/slope/drain/vent requirements, owner/project metadata, source notes, assumptions, diagnostics, and provenance; public examples must be invented or cleared.

ModelStateRecord is a named immutable model snapshot record with tags, notes, external references, assumptions, warnings, analysis-status references, deterministic hashes, provenance, and read-only snapshot semantics; states are review/reproducibility records, not approval/certification/sealing/authentication/code-compliance states.
Node is an addressable point with unit-aware coordinates and six-degree-of-freedom state fields; missing imposed values or constraints are findings, not silent defaults.
Element is an analytical member connecting node references with material, section, optional component, governed local-coordinate, and result-station hooks.
Straight-pipe Element local-coordinate metadata requires a y_reference orientation basis and may carry provenance; local_x_axis is not part of the canonical schema.

FrameKernel is the Rust mechanics module for two-node 3D frame stiffness, local/global transforms, dense assembly, boundary-condition reduction, and temporary dense solve verification; sparse solver selection, canonical calculation units, conversion constants, and downstream adapters remain TBD.
StraightPipeElement is the Rust mechanics module that adapts explicit straight-pipe section and mass properties into the frame-kernel element boundary and recovers local mechanical element forces.

LinearSupport is the Rust mechanics-boundary module for anchors, guides, line stops, vertical supports, linear springs, and imposed displacement data mapped to frame-kernel DOFs; nonlinear gap/lift-off/one-way/friction behavior is out of scope.

NonlinearSupportActiveSet is the Rust mechanics module that classifies one-way, gap/lift-off/contact, and friction-limited support states during nonlinear support iterations; it records active-set changes and nonconvergence diagnostics but does not assemble the global nonlinear solve.
SolverDiagnostics is the Rust mechanics-diagnostics module mapping frame-kernel errors and solver state facts to deterministic diagnostic codes, severities, sources, and statuses.

SolverPerformanceHarness is the Rust observer/regression module that runs invented or public-permissive frame fixtures repeatedly and records matrix metrics, residuals, repeatability deltas, conditioning observations, provenance, assumptions, and limitations.

PrimitiveLoadCase is the Rust mechanics module for weight, pressure, thermal, imposed-displacement, hydrotest, wind, seismic, and occasional primitive load categories; it prepares explicit nodal, element-uniform, and imposed-displacement solver-boundary contributions.

LoadCaseAlgebra is the Rust mechanics-boundary module for user-defined linear combinations, result-state subtraction, and range envelopes over compatible load/result quantities; it preserves unit/dimension intent and analysis statuses.

UserLoadApplication is the Rust mechanics-boundary module for concentrated forces, concentrated moments, and uniform distributed user loads; it prepares explicit solver-boundary contributions and result-recovery hooks.

StressRecovery is the Rust mechanics module that recovers axial, bending, torsional, and pressure membrane stress components from explicit resultants and section/pressure inputs; it does not provide design-code equations, allowables, stress indices, or SIF/flexibility factors.

RulePack is a user-owned schema-governed artifact defining required inputs, declarative formula slots, user-supplied value slots, user-rule check definitions, provenance, redistribution status, diagnostics, checksums, and professional-boundary flags; the schema defines structure only.

ExpressionEvaluator is the Rust rule-pack module that evaluates explicit declarative expression trees with variable bindings, dimension metadata, comparisons, and deterministic findings; it does not parse arbitrary text or execute host-language code.

RulePackLifecycle is the Rust rule-pack module that records lifecycle metadata, privacy/redistribution status, protected-content review state, checksum records, and audit-manifest references; it hashes caller-supplied canonical payload bytes and emits lifecycle findings.

RulePackCompletenessCheck is the Rust rule-pack module that compares required-input declarations with supplied input evidence; it emits deterministic rule-check-blocking findings and RULE_INPUTS_INCOMPLETE readiness without evaluating formulas.

MechanicsBenchmark is a Rust validation fixture and hand-calculation record for open mechanics behavior such as cantilever response, frame assembly, thermal growth, imposed displacement, and stiffness transforms; fixtures must be original/public/permissive with provenance.

StressRecoveryBenchmark is a Rust validation fixture and hand-calculation record for code-neutral stress recovery behavior; stress range is not a fatigue check, allowable comparison, code compliance decision, or professional approval.

Component is a piping-specific object such as bend, elbow, branch, reducer, valve, flange, expansion joint, rigid, specialty, or other user-defined component; user modifiers and code/manufacturer values require provenance and may be private.

Material is a user/private or permissively sourced material record with unit-bearing properties, allowable slots, completeness findings, and provenance; the public schema does not provide protected material allowables, code tables, or proprietary catalog values.
Section is a pipe/section record with unit-bearing properties and provenance; protected dimensional tables and proprietary catalog data are not public defaults.

SectionLibrary holds governed section records with user-entered dimensions, derived-property slots, completeness findings, provenance, and review status; public fixtures remain schema-shape-only or invented unless public-permissive source review is complete.

SectionPropertyCalculation is a derived pipe section and mass-property result calculated from user-entered OD, wall, corrosion, density, contents, and insulation inputs; the calculator does not supply dimensional tables, unit conversion constants, material defaults, or catalog values.

ComponentLibrary holds governed component records for bends, branches, reducers, valves, flanges, expansion joints, rigid parts, specialty items, and user-defined components; SIFs, flexibility factors, manufacturer values, weights, COGs, stiffnesses, and movement limits require provenance and may be private.

LibraryImportProvenanceCheck is an import-boundary validation result for material, section, and component library payloads; it records accept/reject/review/quarantine outcomes without making legal conclusions or publishing private/protected values.

BendElbowComponent is a bend or elbow component record with user-entered centerline geometry, orientation metadata, source references, and user-supplied SIF/flexibility slots; public records define slots and diagnostics only.

BranchConnectionComponent is a branch connection component record with user-entered run/header geometry, connection angle/type slots, reinforcement references, and user-supplied SIF/flexibility slots; public records define slots and diagnostics only.

RigidComponent is a valve, flange, reducer, rigid, or specialty component record with user-entered dimensions, connection references, weight, center-of-gravity, stiffness behavior, and source references; public records define slots and diagnostics only.

ExpansionJointComponent is an expansion joint record with user/manufacturer-supplied stiffness, effective-area, movement-limit, hardware, and manufacturer-reference slots; public records define slots and diagnostics only.
Support is a restraint/support record with target reference, directions, unit-bearing properties, and active-state result hook; nonlinear solution behavior and convergence semantics are solver-owned.

ViewportEditorSession is a schema-first viewport/editor contract for transient camera, hover, selection, drag, snap, view primitives, diagnostics, and application-service command intents over centerline model objects; viewport edits are command intents, not direct persisted-project mutations.

ViewportCommandIntent is a GUI-generated intent for creating nodes, connecting pipe runs, inserting bend/branch/component symbols, and changing selection through an application-service boundary; intents are unit-aware validation requests and undo/redo candidates where reversible.

LoadCase is a primitive loading record with strict typed load-record entries, target references, units, dimensions, and provenance; canonical load records are limited to nodal_force, nodal_moment, element_point_force, and element_uniform_distributed_force.
Combination is an algebraic grouping of load-case factors with an explicit basis; no public code-specific combination defaults are implied.

RulePackRef is a reference to a user/public rule-pack by identity, version, checksum, source notice, redistribution status, and required-input links; rule formulas, protected interpretations, and evaluator implementation are outside this schema.
Quantity is a unit-bearing value record with magnitude, unit, dimension, and provenance; dimensionless values must be explicit and missing or incompatible units are findings, not hidden defaults.
Provenance is a source, license, contributor, redistribution, and review-status record used by reliance-affecting public/private data; unknown or suspected protected sources must remain reviewable.

Reference is a typed stable-object reference used instead of positional coupling where editing, solving, reporting, or audit depends on identity; external references remain explicit and do not bypass schema validation.

Assumption is an explicit unresolved or resolved model assumption with affected references and provenance; assumptions are review evidence and cannot silently become defaults or professional acceptance.

TraceabilityLink is a directed source/target trace record for physical-to-analytical transformation, operation application, state snapshots, analysis runs, comparisons, handoff records, or external references; it does not prove external validation, certification, or code compliance.

Diagnostic is a result-envelope warning/finding record with code, class, severity, source, affected object, message, remediation, and provenance; diagnostics expose missing data and boundary risks without becoming compliance claims.

Checksum is a hash metadata record with algorithm, canonicalization, payload reference, and value; JSON payload hashes use the JCS-compatible basis where applicable and SCA-003 local SQLite storage is not the authoritative hash basis.

ProjectPersistenceEnvelope is a versioned create/open/save envelope with schema version, project payload, migration status, hash metadata, diagnostics, round-trip manifest, validation profile, and service-operation contract records; it delegates model structure to schemas/model.schema.yaml.

PersistenceOperation is an application-service contract record for create, open, save, validate, version-check, and migrate operations; operations must not bypass schema, unit, provenance, rule-pack reference, private-data, protected-content, or professional-boundary checks.

RoundTripManifest is a persistence comparison record naming semantic equality categories, serialization basis, volatile fields, and normalization rules; round trips preserve engineering-relevant data and do not insert silent defaults.

HumanAcceptanceRef is an external human-review or project-acceptance reference bound to specific hashes; it invalidates on bound-hash changes and is not an automatic software approval, certification, sealing, authentication, or code-compliance status.
Result is a mechanical, diagnostic, stress, reaction, or user-rule-check result envelope with analysis statuses and unit-aware values; result statuses do not mean automatic code compliance.

AuditManifest is a reproducibility record for model/input hashes, solver version stamp, unit-system reference, rule-pack checksum refs, asset hashes, privacy/redaction metadata, and manifest findings; it records evidence for review without storing private payloads.

ReportSettings is a report configuration for manifests, provenance summaries, notices, result references, and rule-pack references; report rendering and professional acceptance records remain separate workflows.

Report is an auditable report-facing record for manifests, hashes, statuses, diagnostics, rule-pack refs, provenance summary, and professional-boundary notice; reports are decision support and must not claim certification, sealing, or professional approval by the software.

CalculationReportEnvelope is a schema-first calculation-report assembly contract for model input summary, load cases, result exports, audit manifests, report sections, rule-pack refs, diagnostics, template slots, limitations, and professional-boundary notices; runtime behavior and styling remain TBD.

ReportProtectedContentLintRun is a schema-first linter configuration, target, finding, summary, and provenance contract for public report templates, examples, and fixtures; it is deterministic heuristic review evidence only and does not provide legal clearance or code-compliance proof.

ReportSectionEnvelope holds schema-first records for report-facing warnings, analysis-status disclosures, assumptions, limitations, user-supplied values, provenance notes, unresolved TBDs, and human-review-needed findings; full rendering and final layout remain TBD.

ResultExportEnvelope is a schema-first JSON result export contract for review, regression comparison, reports, headless automation, and governed downstream tooling; it preserves units, diagnostics, provenance, hashes, and status boundaries with no professional/code-compliance claims.

HeadlessRunnerEnvelope is a schema-first request/result contract for non-GUI solve execution, benchmark automation, regression execution, audit-manifest capture, and result-export handoff; CLI syntax, CI provider, and release matrix remain TBD.

AdapterFrameworkEnvelope is a schema-first format-neutral contract for import/export adapter declarations, validation plans, diagnostics, provenance, privacy, checksum/audit refs, result-envelope compatibility, and no-bypass controls; adapters cannot bypass units, provenance, privacy, or protected-content screening.

Companion schema schemas/section.schema.yaml defines section-library metadata, pipe/section dimension slots, derived-property slots, completeness findings, provenance, and review status; protected dimensional tables and proprietary catalog values are not public defaults.

Companion schema schemas/component.schema.yaml defines component-library metadata, user-entered dimension/weight/COG/stiffness/modifier slots, completeness findings, provenance, and review status; protected SIF/flexibility tables and code-specific values are user-supplied or separately reviewed.

Companion schema schemas/design_knowledge.schema.json defines schema-first design knowledge records for endpoints, line data, corridors, zones, equipment interfaces, requirements, owner/project metadata, source notes, assumptions, diagnostics, and provenance; user/project supplied only.

Companion schema schemas/model_state.schema.json defines schema-first immutable model state records with state metadata, external references, assumptions, warnings, hashes, provenance, and read-only snapshot semantics; human acceptance remains external and hash-bound.

Companion schema schemas/analysis_boundary.schema.yaml separates mechanics solve authority, user-rule-check authority, missing-input findings, diagnostics, and external human acceptance references; human acceptance is reference-only and hash-bound.
Companion schema schemas/analysis_status.schema.yaml defines result-envelope status semantics and external human acceptance records; HUMAN_APPROVED_FOR_PROJECT is not an automatic software status.

Companion schema schemas/project_persistence.schema.yaml defines the versioned project persistence envelope, round-trip manifest, migration status, hash metadata, validation profile, service operations, private-data markers, and external human acceptance references.

Companion schema schemas/rule_pack.schema.yaml defines rule-pack metadata, public/private classification, required inputs, declarative formula slots, user-supplied value slots, check definitions, diagnostics, provenance, redistribution status, checksums, and professional-boundary controls.

Companion schema schemas/report_generator.schema.yaml defines schema-first calculation-report envelopes, template slots, rendered-section metadata, source envelope references, audit/hash refs, rule-pack refs, diagnostics, provenance, privacy classification, and unresolved runtime/reporting TBDs.

Companion schema schemas/report_protected_content_linter.schema.yaml defines schema-first protected-content linter configuration, public-surface targets, findings, source locations, review routes, dispositions, summaries, and provenance; it is heuristic review evidence only.

Companion schema schemas/report_sections.schema.yaml defines schema-first report-section records for diagnostics, analysis-status disclosures, provenance notes, user-supplied values, assumptions, limitations, unresolved TBDs, and professional-boundary controls.

Companion schema schemas/results.schema.yaml defines schema-first JSON result export envelopes for result identity, model/run references, unit-aware values, diagnostics, provenance, reproducibility refs, analysis status, rule-pack refs, and downstream-use declarations.

Companion schema schemas/viewport_editor.schema.yaml defines schema-first viewport/editor status, camera/transient state, view primitives, selection, diagnostics, provenance, professional-boundary controls, and command intents for centerline editing.

Companion schema schemas/headless_runner.schema.yaml defines the schema-first headless runner request/result envelope for operation identity, project/model/unit/load/input-manifest references, requested outputs, job progress/cancellation, diagnostics, result-export refs, audit-manifest refs, privacy, provenance, and professional-boundary controls.

Companion schema schemas/adapter_framework.schema.yaml defines schema-first format-neutral adapter framework envelopes for adapter capability declarations, validation plans, operation results, diagnostics, provenance, privacy, checksum/audit refs, result-envelope compatibility, and no-bypass controls; it does not authorize direct SQL access.
Lifecycle states for development deliverables progress OPEN to INITIALIZED to IN_PROGRESS to CHECKING to ISSUED.
ISSUED means accepted as a development artifact by the human project authority; it does not mean professional engineering authentication of any piping calculation.
